questions.q: What did Yahweh promise Joshua concerning Jericho, its king, and its warriors?
questions.a: Yahweh promised Joshua that he had given Jericho, its king, and its warriors into Joshua’s hand.

questions.q: How were the men of war to circle the city of Jericho for six days?
questions.a: All the men of war were to circle the city, going around it one time each day for six days.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Joshua should happen on the seventh day involving priests, shofars, and the people?
questions.a: Yahweh told him that seven priests should carry seven shofars before the Box, and on the seventh day the people should circle the city seven times while the priests blew the shofars; then, at a long blast, all the people should shout.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to the city wall when the people shouted on the seventh day?
questions.a: Yahweh said the wall of the city would collapse unto itself, and the people should go up, every man straight into the city.

questions.q: What did Joshua command the people not to do until he told them to shout?
questions.a: Joshua commanded the people not to shout, nor let their voice be heard, nor let a word go out of their mouth until the day he told them to shout.

questions.q: Who did Joshua say would live when the city of Jericho was devoted to Yahweh, and why?
questions.a: Joshua said that only Rahab the prostitute and all who were with her in her house would live, because she hid the messengers they sent.

questions.q: What did Joshua declare was holy to Yahweh and must enter Yahweh’s treasury?
questions.a: Joshua declared that all the silver, gold, and objects of bronze and iron were holy to Yahweh and must enter Yahweh’s treasury.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel do to everything in the city after the walls of Jericho fell?
questions.a: The people of Israel devoted to destruction by the sword all that was in the city—men and women, young and old, oxen, sheep, and donkeys.

questions.q: What did Joshua command the two men who had spied out the land to do regarding Rahab?
questions.a: Joshua commanded the two spies to go into the prostitute’s house and bring her out, and all who belonged to her, as they had sworn to her.

questions.q: What curse did Joshua pronounce on the man who would rebuild Jericho?
questions.a: Joshua said that the man who rebuilt Jericho would be cursed before Yahweh: he would lay its foundation with his firstborn and set up its gates with his youngest son.

commentary.text: Jericho is taken, Rahab and her family are saved.

Verses 1–5 Jericho resolves Israel shall not be its master. It shut itself up, being strongly fortified both by art and nature. Thus were they foolish, and their hearts hardened to their destruction; the miserable case of all that strengthen themselves against the Almighty. God resolves Israel shall be its master, and that quickly. No warlike preparations were to be made. By the uncommon method of besieging the city, the Lord honoured the ark, as the symbol of his presence, and showed that all the victories were from him. The faith and patience of the people were proved and increased.

Wherever the ark went, the people attended it. God's ministers, by the trumpet of the everlasting gospel, which proclaims liberty and victory, must encourage the followers of Christ in their spiritual warfare. As promised deliverances must be expected in God's way, so they must be expected in his time. At last the people were to shout: they did so, and the walls fell. This was a shout of faith; they believed the walls of Jericho would fall. It was a shout of prayer; they cry to Heaven for help, and help came.

Jericho was to be a solemn and awful sacrifice to the justice of God, upon those who had filled up the measure of their sins. So He appoints, from whom, as creatures, they received their lives, and to whom, as sinners, they had forfeited them. Rahab perished not with them that believed not, Heb 11:31. All her kindred were saved with her; thus faith in Christ brings salvation to the house, Ac 16:31. She, and they with her, were plucked as brands from the burning. With Rahab, or with the men of Jericho; our portion must be assigned, as we posses or disregard the sign of salvation; even faith in Christ, which worketh by love. Let us remember what depends upon our choice, and let us choose accordingly. God shows the weight of a Divine curse; where it rests there is no getting from under it; for it brings ruin without remedy.
